summary: Reviewed 5 files (2 production, 3 test). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium findings. 2 Low/Info observations recorded. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Low | A02 (Cryptographic Failures) | MysqlDumpBackupService.cs BuildStartInfo: Password is passed as a single ArgumentList entry ('-p{password}'). While this prevents shell injection, the combined flag+value form means the credential is visible in Windows process command-line listings (Task Manager, Sysinternals Process Monitor). For a local desktop single-user application this is Low severity — the user already holds the credential. Remediation if desired: use '--password' from a temp file or environment variable via Process.Environment, though this adds complexity. No action required for current scope.

Info | A08 (Software & Data Integrity) | MysqlDumpBackupService.cs BackupAsync: mysqldumpPath is constructed from a user-configured 'MySqlBinaryFolder' setting. A tampered settings file could redirect execution to a malicious binary. This is inherent to any external-tool integration pattern and is Info severity for a local desktop app where the attacker would need user-level filesystem write access already. No action required.

Info | A03 (Injection) — defence-in-depth confirmed: ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList used exclusively (psi.Arguments stays empty, verified by test BuildStartInfo_DoesNotUseArgumentsStringForm). SanitizeDatabaseName strips Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars() including '/' and '\', preventing path traversal via the filename component. Path.Combine(destinationFolder, outputFileName) is safe because outputFileName contains no directory separators post-sanitization. No findings.

comments.note: MysqlDumpBackupService.BackupAsync — on OperationCanceledException, Process.Dispose() is called (via `using`) but Process.Kill() is not. The mysqldump child process will continue running until it encounters a broken-pipe write error on its stdout/stderr, which will cause it to self-terminate. For a local desktop app this is low severity and self-correcting, but explicit kill before the re-throw would be cleaner resource management. Suggested addition in the OCE catch: `try { process.Kill(entireProcessTree: false); } catch { }` before the file cleanup.

SanitizeDatabaseName: Array.IndexOf linear search over the ~9-41 platform invalid-char array is correct and readable for a once-per-backup call. A HashSet<char> would be semantically clearer for 'membership test' intent and O(1), but the performance difference is immeasurable at this call frequency. No action required — flagged for awareness only.

[documentation-forward] IDatabaseBackupService.BackupAsync XML doc should explicitly state that OperationCanceledException propagates to the caller on cancellation. The project has a documented pattern (ILibraryScanner.RefreshAsync) that swallows OCE and returns normally — BackupAsync deviates from that pattern intentionally (cancellation of a backup should be visible to the AsyncRelayCommand infrastructure). Documenting this exception: '<exception cref="OperationCanceledException">Thrown when <paramref name="cancellationToken"/> is cancelled. Any partially-written output file is deleted before the exception propagates.</exception>' would prevent future maintainers from assuming the swallow-pattern applies here.
